en: The Sūtra of One Hundred and Eight Names of the Holy Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Mingjiao Dashi Tianxizai of Jalandhara in Central India during the Song Dynasty, by Imperial Decree.
Thus have I heard.
At one time the Buddha was staying on Mount Potalaka, in the palace of the noble Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
The mountain peak rose loftily, composed of various precious gems.
There is stainless, pure Jāmbūnada gold,
various precious jewels such as the king of maṇi gems,
and the wondrous radiance of their colors constantly shines everywhere; furthermore, there are celestial kalpa-trees that grant all wishes.
At all times, there flow forth incalculable numbers of *surabhi* (celestial) perfumes,
sandalwood, aloeswood, and *kusuma* flowers,
which are soft, pleasant, and agreeable to the mind.
Exquisite forms and fragrances adorned every place. Furthermore,
immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of devas,
nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans went to where the Buddha was, prostrating themselves with their heads at his feet in worship.
They made offerings, paid homage, showed respect, and offered praise;
with single-minded devotion and palms joined, they listened to the Dharma in silence.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Brahma King, saying:
The Tathāgata’s teaching of the Dharma is excellent in the beginning, middle, and end;
its meaning is profound and far-reaching, and its phrasing is skillful.
It is pure, unadulterated, perfect, and the manifestation of the completely purified holy life (*brahmacarya*).
He teaches the Dharma according to what is appropriate to benefit sentient beings.
These are the one hundred and eight names of the Noble Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
If there are those who hear them, they shall not fall into the evil realms for hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of countless kalpas.
If that person has committed any of the five deeds of immediate retribution, they shall all be completely eliminated.
In every life and every birth, they shall attain the knowledge of past lives.
The secret mantra of the one hundred and eight names of the Noble Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva is as follows:

Māraṇa-narendra-nimantrita. At that time...
The Buddha addressed Brahmā and Śakra, saying:
"If there be anyone who upholds, recites, and reads this secret vidyā of the One Hundred and Eight Names of the Holy Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva..."
It should be known that such a person will, in every successive birth throughout their lives,
always behold the Noble Avalokiteśvara;
if they constantly uphold [this practice], they will attain great wealth and nobility.
One attains intelligence; one attains valor;
one attains physical beauty; one attains a sublime voice;
and one attains eloquence.
One will attain constant knowledge of the meaning of all dharmas and entry into the maṇḍala.
Whatever prayers one makes, all mantra-siddhis will be accomplished.
By reciting this daily at dawn, one will forever be free from the suffering of illness, scabies, and chronic respiratory ailments.
At the time of death, one will be reborn in the Western World of Ultimate Bliss.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Brahma King, saying:
"If a person receives and upholds the names of as many Buddhas as there are grains of sand in sixty-two billion Ganges Rivers..."
Furthermore, if one were able to provide the four types of offerings throughout their entire life, would the karmic fruit obtained by that person be great?
Brahmā King replied: "It would be very much so, World-Honored One; it would be very much so, Sugata."
The Buddha said: "If a person upholds the one hundred and eight names of the Noble Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara,
or even for a brief moment pays homage and makes offerings,
the karmic fruit of these two persons is exactly equal and without distinction."
Brahmā, you should know that by receiving, upholding, reading, and reciting the One Hundred and Eight Names of the Noble Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara,
one shall obtain such benefits as these immeasurable and boundless rewards of merit.
How much more so for those who, throughout their entire lives, uphold, maintain, read, and recite it;
the merit they obtain will be inexhaustible life after life, birth after birth.
When the World-Honored One had spoken these words, [the assembly rejoiced].
Mahābrahmā, Śakra Devendra,
the eight classes of devas and nāgas, and the entire great assembly,
having heard what the Buddha taught, believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.
